title: Chiral Dynamics of an Intruder across Dilute and Hydrodynamic Regimes
abstract: We introduce and simulate an analytically tractable model for an intruder of arbitrary shape in a nonequilibrium bath, with chirality originating from the bath, the intruder, or their coupling. In the dilute regime, a Langevin description derived from a Boltzmann-Lorentz equation shows how intruder geometry governs ratchet effects and odd response. In the dense regime, the dynamics of the intruder are instead governed by the hydrodynamic modes of the bath and edge currents, which are described by a Stokes equation including a chiral torque density. Our results link shape to chiral transport and show that odd response arises from distinct mechanisms in the dilute and dense limits.
summary: This work develops a comprehensive model to study how chirality affects the motion of an object (intruder) moving through a fluctuating bath. It successfully bridges two distinct physical regimes—the dilute gas limit and the dense hydrodynamic limit—by showing that the source of chiral transport changes fundamentally between these limits.
main_problem: The study investigates how chiral dynamics of an intruder are governed by its geometry when moving through a non-equilibrium bath, comparing results across dilute and dense hydrodynamic regimes.
main_result: The odd response (chirality) arises from distinct mechanisms in the dilute limit (fluctuation-driven) versus the dense limit (hydrodynamic edge currents), leading to a density-controlled crossover in dynamics.
method: Theoretical derivation using Boltzmann-Lorentz equations, followed by approximations yielding Langevin descriptions, and comparison with molecular dynamics simulations.
model_or_system: The system consists of an intruder of arbitrary shape immersed in a non-equilibrium bath of point particles. Chirality can be introduced via the bath, the intruder, or their coupling mechanisms.
key_observables: Odd diffusivity ($D_{odd}$), rotational damping ($\Gamma$), and the torque generated by chiral edge currents.
important_parameters: Bath density ($n_b$), restitution coefficient ($\alpha$), and the degree of chirality ($\Delta$).
main_assumptions: The Langevin equation is valid when bath-particle inertia is small compared to intruder inertia; in the dense limit, continuum approximations are used.
figures_summary: Figures compare parameters for different shapes (wheel vs. triangle) and illustrate how even/odd diffusivities change with bath density, showing deviations from dilute theory at finite density.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the collision rules, deriving the Langevin equation in the dilute limit via Boltzmann-Lorentz analysis, and then extending the framework to the dense hydrodynamic regime where edge currents dominate the torque generation.
why_interesting: It provides a detailed theoretical mapping between microscopic collision dynamics (Boltzmann) and macroscopic continuum fluid mechanics (Stokes/hydrodynamics), which is crucial for understanding non-equilibrium transport in complex media.
